skills: Anthropic's AI workbench for rigorous science. Source: https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/overview
Install Claude Science on macOS, Windows, or Linux, sign in with your Claude account, and run your first analysis. Source: https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/get-started
Claude Science in its own window on macOS
Keep working when Claude Science switches to its own window on a Mac: open, quit, and update it, and turn macOS permissions back on. Source: https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/mac-app-window

Install the latest version of Claude Science on Mac, Windows, or Linux, and get past an Update required message or an update that fails. Source: https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/update-claude-science
A project groups related sessions and the artifacts they produce. Source: https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/core-concepts
Auto mode lets Claude Science run code and call connectors without stopping to ask about every step. Source: https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/auto-mode
Use Claude Science on more than one computer
What to expect when you sign in on another computer, or under another sign-in on the same computer. Source: https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/multiple-computers

Artifacts in Claude Science are files Claude saves into a project, such as figures, datasets, and reports. Open, version, trace, and delete them. Source: https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/artifacts

Comments in Claude Science pin a note to a specific part of an artifact, such as selected text or a point on a figure, and send the note to Claude. Source: https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/comments

A built-in verification step that independently re-reads Claude's recent responses, the approved plan, saved artifacts, and the execution record, then checks whether its claims match what ran. Source: https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/the-reviewer
Run on a remote Linux server
Install Claude Science on a cloud VM or lab server and use it from your own browser through an SSH tunnel. Source: https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/run-on-remote-linux-server
Claude writes and runs Python, R, and shell commands. Source: https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/tools-and-environments
Connectors give Claude access to external data sources during an analysis. Source: https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/connectors-and-skills
Connect a machine you can reach over SSH (a lab workstation or an HPC login node) so Claude can run jobs on it. Source: https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/remote-compute-clusters

Claude Science can run jobs on an external cloud provider you control, and connect to model servers that serve scientific models over HTTP. Source: https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/compute-providers
Connect Amazon S3, Google Cloud Storage, or Azure Blob Storage so Claude can read data and write results in place, with your permission. Source: https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/cloud-storage

Claude retrieves open-access full text without credentials; add publisher keys or a library proxy to reach paywalled text you're entitled to. Source: https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/literature-access
Add any Model Context Protocol (MCP) server as a Remote (HTTPS web server) or Local command (program on your computer). Source: https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/custom-connectors
Browse nine example prompts from nine fields of science, each the start of a complete analysis in Claude Science. Source: https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/example-gallery
Genetic drift in a bottle: Buri's 107 fruit-fly populations
Simulate 107 bottles of 16 fruit flies drifting by chance alone and compare them with Peter Buri's real bottles (1956). Source: https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/example-gallery/bio-drift
A titration curve from the full equilibrium: which indicator finds the equivalence point?
Solve the full equilibrium for 25.0 mL of 0.100 M acetic acid as 0.100 M NaOH is added, without the usual shortcuts. Source: https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/example-gallery/chem-titration
A first Kaplan–Meier curve: the 1963 leukemia trial of 6-MP
Compare 6-MP against placebo with Kaplan–Meier curves from 42 remission times typed into the prompt. Source: https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/example-gallery/clin-km
PageRank on a web of 11 pages: why 1 good link beats 6 weak ones

Follow a random surfer on Wikipedia's 11-page example until the numbers settle, and reproduce all 11 published values to 0.1 point. Source: https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/example-gallery/cs-pagerank-tiny
A first finite-element model: a clamped steel ruler bends and vibrates

Split a 300 mm steel ruler clamped at one end into 4 beam elements and check its bending under 1 N and its first 3 vibration modes against beam theory. Source: https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/example-gallery/eng-beam
A first X-ray diffraction pattern: why silicon shows 6 peaks and salt 9
Simulate the X-ray powder patterns of silicon and table salt and label every peak with Bragg's law. Source: https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/example-gallery/mat-xrd
The Ulam spiral: are the primes' diagonal streaks real?
Compare the share of primes per diagonal on Ulam's 1963 spiral of 1 to 40,401 against as many random odd numbers. Source: https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/example-gallery/math-ulam
The double slit, one electron at a time

Rebuild the picture of Tonomura's 1989 experiment with an ideal double slit: each electron lands as 1 random dot, yet fringes 10.7 µm apart build up. Source: https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/example-gallery/phys-doubleslit
Schelling's segregation model: ask for 30% same-color neighbors, end up with 75%

Ask for 30% same-color neighbors, end up with about 75%: the textbook computer version of Thomas Schelling's 1971 idea. Source: https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/example-gallery/soc-schelling-small

What happens when a model's safeguards flag a message, how to switch models automatically, and how to choose a use case under the Life Sciences Verification Program (beta). Source: https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/safeguards

Fix errors you see while using Claude Science: being signed out, capacity retries, Agent Failed, environment setup, connectors, dictation, and updates. Source: https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/troubleshooting
One-sentence definitions for the terms you meet in Claude Science, from artifact to workspace. Source: https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/glossary

Reference for the claude-science command: its subcommands, the serve flags, the single-use login link, and the environment variables you can set. Source: https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/command-line-settings

Claude Science's config.toml file: where it lives, how it interacts with Settings, and its network, web search, and upload keys. Source: https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/configuration-file-reference
Release notes for Claude Science, including new features, improvements, and bug fixes by version. Source: https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/changelog
Legal agreements, compliance certifications, and security information for Claude Science. Source: https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/legal-and-compliance

How to run Claude Science behind an outbound proxy, a TLS-inspecting proxy, an internal package mirror, and an egress firewall, with the settings your network team needs for each. Source: https://claude.com/docs/claude-science/corporate-networks
